clear.oewn-01754557-s.tone: Goes beyond flaws and marks to anything mixed in that spoils it, so it can describe a substance, not only a performance.
clear.oewn-01754557-s.reasoning: 'Blemish' became 'marks' and 'impurity' became 'anything mixed in that spoils it'. I kept the old claim that it reaches further than flaw and blemish, and the point that it fits a substance as well as a performance. I also replaced the odd 'clear a substance' with 'describe'.

consummate.oewn-01754870-s.tone: Formal where *complete* is plain, and it turns having every needed quality into the highest kind of praise.
consummate.oewn-01754870-s.reasoning: 'Superlative' and 'accolade' became 'the highest kind of praise', and 'total sufficiency' became 'having every needed quality', which follows the gloss. I kept the formal-versus-plain contrast with *complete*. The note still fits a charge of +3.

incorrupted.oewn-01755331-s.tone: Treats being without fault as something kept whole rather than achieved, and sounds stiffer than *faultless*.
incorrupted.oewn-01755331-s.reasoning: 'In a stiffer register' became 'sounds stiffer', which removes the grammar term. 'Intact' became 'kept whole'. I kept both the kept-versus-achieved framing and the comparison with *faultless*.

unflawed.oewn-01755578-s.tone: Simply says there is no flaw, without the admiration that *flawless* carries.
unflawed.oewn-01755578-s.reasoning: 'The plain negation' became 'simply says there is no flaw', which removes the grammar term. I kept the contrast: *flawless* carries admiration and this word does not.

homelike.oewn-00479651-s.tone: Praises a place for feeling like home and putting you at ease, where *cozy* praises its warmth.
homelike.oewn-00479651-s.reasoning: The old note was 26 words. I kept what it said: the comfort comes from the feeling of home and from putting you at ease, and it is set against *cozy*'s warmth. I only tightened the wording.

displeased.oewn-01811138-a.tone: The coolest word here: it names a lack of pleasure, felt or shown, without any heat in it.
displeased.oewn-01811138-a.reasoning: The verb 'registers' was the problem, so the word now 'names'. 'Without conceding any heat' became 'without any heat in it'. The old 'lets it show' covered only half of the gloss, so I wrote 'felt or shown' to match its 'experiencing or manifesting'. The note still fits a charge of 0.

miffed.oewn-01811355-s.tone: Light: it treats the feeling as a small thing and the person as easily upset, where *annoyed* judges neither.
miffed.oewn-01811355-s.reasoning: The old note was 29 words. I kept both judgements it described, a small feeling and an easily upset person, and the contrast with *annoyed*, which judges neither. Writing 'the feeling' refers to the gloss's impatience or anger without restating it or dropping either half.

pissed.oewn-01811355-s.tone: Rude and blunt: the crudest way in this group to say it, and everything *displeased* holds back.
pissed.oewn-01811355-s.reasoning: 'In the coarsest register the family has' became 'the crudest way in this group to say it', and 'vulgar' became 'rude'. I kept the contrast: this word says openly everything *displeased* holds back.

roiled.oewn-01811355-s.tone: Churning, not flaring: the feeling is muddy and unsettled all through, where *stung* is one sharp point.
roiled.oewn-01811355-s.reasoning: 'Turbid' became 'muddy', which is the stirred-up water behind the word. 'The impatience or anger' became 'the feeling', so neither half of the gloss is lost. I kept the churn-versus-flare image and the contrast with *stung*'s one sharp point.

stung.oewn-01811355-s.tone: Something landed, and the feeling is the sudden pull back from it, where *irritated* only wears on.
stung.oewn-01811355-s.reasoning: 'Flinch' and 'recoil' became 'the sudden pull back', and 'impatience or anger' became 'the feeling'. I kept the image of a blow landing and a reaction to it, and the contrast with *irritated*, which only wears on.

cheesed_off.oewn-01811732-s.tone: British, and it takes the drama out: patience fully lost, in a phrase too casual to shout, where *exasperated* keeps its calm.
cheesed_off.oewn-01811732-s.reasoning: 'Deflating' became 'takes the drama out', 'offhand' became 'casual' and 'composure' became 'calm'. I kept 'British', the complete loss of patience, and the contrast with *exasperated*.

disgusted.oewn-01811926-s.tone: Strong dislike from having had too much of something - the stomach turning, not anger aimed at anyone.
disgusted.oewn-01811926-s.reasoning: 'Distaste' became 'dislike' and 'surfeited' became 'having had too much'. The old note made two comparisons. I kept the one the gloss supports best, too-much versus anger aimed at someone, and dropped 'the family's furthest recoil'. The charge of -3 still carries that strength.

inspired.oewn-01125269-s.tone: Milder than *divine* and *elysian*: it credits the excellence to something breathed in from outside, but names no gods.
inspired.oewn-01125269-s.reasoning: The old note was 25 words. 'The mildest of the three' became 'milder than *divine* and *elysian*', which keeps both neighbours. I kept the breathed-in-from-outside image and the point that it does not name the gods.

implicit.oewn-00944754-a.tone: Neutral, covering both a meaning never spelled out and one that sits in a thing's nature, where *unspoken* covers only the first.
implicit.oewn-00944754-a.reasoning: The old note was 27 words. I kept both halves of the gloss, never said and part of a thing's nature, and the contrast with *unspoken*, which covers only the first. I dropped only the extra label 'two-sided', because 'both' says the same.

inexplicit.oewn-00944754-a.tone: Built as 'not explicit', it sees the telling as falling short, where *implicit* sees a quality of the thing itself.
inexplicit.oewn-00944754-a.reasoning: 'Built as a negation' became 'built as "not explicit"', which removes the grammar term. 'A shortfall in the telling' became 'the telling falling short', and 'property' became 'quality'. I kept the contrast with *implicit*. The note still fits a charge of -1.

implicit_in.oewn-00945209-s.tone: A linking phrase, not a quality: it must name what the meaning lies in, which *inherent* and *underlying* need not.
implicit_in.oewn-00945209-s.reasoning: The old note was 26 words and used the grammar word 'adjectives'. I named the neighbours it meant, *inherent* and *underlying*, instead. 'Relational' became 'linking' and 'lodged' became 'lies'. I kept the one difference the note drew: this phrase has to name what the meaning lies in.

unverbalized.oewn-00945649-s.tone: Sounds clinical: the gap is a failure to put something into words, not a silence with any weight to it.
unverbalized.oewn-00945649-s.reasoning: 'Clinical in register' became 'sounds clinical'. I kept 'clinical' because the note for *unverbalised* uses the same word and no everyday phrase means quite the same. 'Convert into words' became 'put into words'. I kept the contrast with a silence that carries weight.

intrusive.oewn-01354915-a.tone: The plain word for the fault: it names the pushing-in itself, without the scorn in *meddlesome*.
intrusive.oewn-01354915-a.reasoning: The old note was 25 words and made two comparisons. The contrast with *meddlesome* is the safer one to keep. The gloss's 'upon privacy' is itself close to the trespass idea, so saying this word lacks *encroaching*'s trespass sat less securely. 'Contempt' became 'scorn'.

encroaching.oewn-01355168-s.tone: It stresses slowness: ground taken bit by bit, so no single step looks like the violation *invasive* makes it sound.
encroaching.oewn-01355168-s.reasoning: The old note was 27 words. I kept the stress on slowness, the ground taken a little at a time, and the contrast with *invasive*. 'A little at a time' became 'bit by bit'. I kept 'violation', because 'wrong' would have been weaker.

infelicitous.oewn-01004300-a.tone: Formal and softened: it calls a thing unsuited to its use and faulty, while sounding sorry about it, where *inept* simply condemns.
infelicitous.oewn-01004300-a.reasoning: 'Misapplied' became 'unsuited to its use', which follows the gloss's 'not appropriate in application'. 'Keeping an apologetic surface' became 'while sounding sorry about it'. I kept both halves of the gloss and the contrast with *inept*.

aspirant.oewn-00105332-s.tone: Formal and cool: it notes the reaching for recognition or advancement without judging it, where *aspiring* sounds warm.
aspirant.oewn-00105332-s.reasoning: The verb 'registers' became 'notes', and 'without any verdict on it' became 'without judging it'. I kept both halves of the gloss and the contrast with the warmer *aspiring*. The note still fits a charge of 0.
